headline: IRAN-ISRAEL HALT ATTACKS — Gold Stuck at 11-Week Low as Markets Stay Skeptical; CPI Wednesday Is the Real Catalyst
snippet: Iran and Israel halted mutual missile and drone strikes Monday following a Trump appeal — the first pause since the early-April ceasefire broke down last weekend — but gold remained muted near its 11-week low of ~$4,330 as traders stayed skeptical about the truce's durability ahead of Wednesday's May CPI print. Oil fell 4% to a seven-week low on the news, removing an energy-inflation risk premium that had compounded rate-hike fears; but with CME FedWatch still pricing a 40–72% probability of a December Fed rate hike after May's blowout payrolls, traders are waiting for the inflation data to determine the next directional move for bullion.

headline: WPG DRILLS 9.06 g/t Au OVER 19.7m AT NE TYRO — 35.7m at 3.2 g/t Au Confirms Zone; Gold Chain Maiden MRE Coming H2 2026
snippet: West Point Gold Corp. (TSXV: WPG; OTCQB: WPGCF) reported June 9 results from the NE Tyro zone at its Gold Chain Project in Yavapai County, Arizona — hole GC26-134 returning 19.7 metres at 9.06 g/t Au from 95.8m and hole GC26-137 returning 35.7 metres at 3.2 g/t Au including 10.2 metres at 10.23 g/t Au from 53.2m. The 2025–2026 campaign of 21,079 total metres (RC and core) is now complete, with ~7,025m of assays still pending; the company is integrating all results toward a maiden NI 43-101 resource estimate expected later in 2026, with NE Tyro's high-grade results materially boosting confidence in the zone's ability to anchor a meaningful resource.

headline: SCORPIO GOLD HITS 6.95 g/t Au OVER 11.98m — Visible Gold at 65.99 g/t Confirms Caldera Volcanics Target at Goldwedge, Nevada
snippet: Scorpio Gold Corp. (TSXV: SGN; OTCQB: SRCRF) released June 9 Phase 2 step-out results from its Manhattan District Project in Nevada — hole 26MN-091 returning 6.95 g/t Au over 11.98 metres from 242.99m depth, including a visible-gold interval of 65.99 g/t Au over 1.16m at 250.76m, within the Caldera Volcanics unit at the Goldwedge target. With 92 holes and 25,919 total metres drilled to date, the campaign continues to outline a spatially large gold system within the Manhattan Caldera, with assays from multiple remaining holes pending and results being compiled toward a resource estimate.

headline: CERRO DE PASCO METALLURGY ADVANCES — 110+ Tests Back Two-Concentrate Flowsheet; Peru Silver-Pyrite Tailings Drilling Approved
snippet: Cerro de Pasco Resources Inc. (TSXV: CDPR; OTC: GPPRF) reported June 9 that its integrated metallurgical test program at the Quiulacocha Tailings Reprocessing Project in Peru — comprising more than 110 individual tests — now supports a two-concentrate flowsheet that separates silver-bearing pyrite and base-metal concentrates using conventional and emerging flotation technologies. Rheology testing confirmed the tailings are pumpable at an optimal 65–75% solids range, clearing a key process engineering gate; Phase 2 drilling permits have been approved and initial drill holes are targeted for mid-2026, advancing the path toward a resource estimate on one of the largest historical tailings facilities in the Peruvian Andes.

headline: MYRIAD URANIUM ACQUIRES 23 BRECCIA-PIPE TARGETS, ARIZONA — Wedgemount Options 75%; Wate Pipe Carries Historical Resource
source_name: Investing News Network / Myriad Uranium Corp
snippet: Myriad Uranium Corp. announced June 9 the acquisition of 15 state mineral leases and 8 split-estate claims covering 5,600 acres in Northern Arizona's historically significant uranium district, hosting 23 breccia-pipe uranium and REE targets — including the Wate Pipe, which carries a historical non-43-101 resource estimate. Simultaneously, Myriad granted Wedgemount Resources Corp. a three-year option to earn up to 75% of the Breccia Pipe Project, fast-tracking exploration on the same breccia-pipe deposit type historically mined at high grades in the Grand Canyon region; two additional state mineral awards are pending, which would expand the total land package to 6,080 acres.

headline: MORGAN STANLEY FLAGS JUNE 30 COPPER TARIFF DEADLINE — 43% Tariff Probability Priced; COMEX Net Longs at All-Time High
snippet: Morgan Stanley has flagged the June 30, 2026 Commerce Department deadline for the Section 232 refined copper tariff review as the single most important near-term risk event for the copper market: a positive recommendation could trigger COMEX pricing approximately 15% above the LME benchmark as domestic demand rotates to U.S.-delivered supply. The bank estimates markets are currently pricing a 43% probability of a 15% duty taking effect in January 2027 (rising to 30% in 2028), with COMEX speculative net-long positioning already at an all-time high — meaning any tariff announcement before month-end could produce amplified price action that directly affects cost models for junior copper developers across North America.

headline: MYANMAR HOLDS 50% OF HEAVY RARE EARTHS — China Dy/Tb Export Controls Active; Physical Access Now the Real Constraint
snippet: Rare Earth Exchanges' June 1–5 weekly recap identifies a structural break in the heavy rare earth market: the Kachin Independence Army controls extraction areas in Myanmar's Kachin State — source of roughly 50% of global dysprosium and terbium supply — while military offensives to recapture mining zones were ongoing through May 2026, creating physical access constraints that some market participants now describe as the binding constraint, not price. China amplified the pressure by implementing export licensing requirements in April on dysprosium/terbium alloys and downstream products incorporating heavy rare earth elements, complicating procurement for EV motor and wind turbine manufacturers dependent on NdFeB permanent magnets that have no commercially viable substitutes at current operating temperatures.

headline: LITHIUM BUST IS OVER — CME Hydroxide Up 86% YTD, Back Above $20K/t; Zimbabwe Ban and Mine Closures Tightened the Market
snippet: Reuters commodities columnist Andy Home argues in a June 5 Mining.com column that lithium's three-year bust is definitively over: the CME lithium hydroxide contract has surged 86% year-to-date to trade back above $20,000 per metric ton — its highest level since late 2023 — driven by Zimbabwe's export ban on raw lithium concentrates (removing ~7% of global supply), widespread mine curtailments from the prior price collapse, and sustained EV and energy-storage demand. The key open question is whether the recovery evolves into a full boom or stabilises: disappointing Q1 global EV sales and the potential for Chinese supply restarts mean the rally has moved ahead of near-term fundamentals, and Home warns volatility will intensify as the structural bull case and the cyclical overhang collide in H2 2026.

headline: METALS FOCUS: GOLD BULL STILL HAS LEGS — H2 Recovery Expected Once War Uncertainty Lifts; Full-Year Average $4,920 Intact
snippet: Independent research firm Metals Focus, in its Gold Focus 2026 annual report summary published June 8 via Money Metals Exchange and GoldSeek, maintains a bullish full-year gold forecast averaging $4,920/oz — arguing the current ~22% pullback from the January 29 all-time high is consistent with normal drawdown patterns inside a primary uptrend, not a cycle reversal. The firm identifies the U.S.–Israel war on Iran (which launched in February and initially drove equity-market dislocations that pushed gold lower against intuition) as the primary overhang, and expects the bull run to resume in H2 2026 once that uncertainty clears; structural demand from central banks, de-dollarisation flows, and fiscal deficit expansion remains intact beneath the rate-shock correction.

headline: JEFFERIES NAMES 4 BUY-RATED MINERS — Capstone Copper, Barrick, Endeavour, Kinross; EPS Upgrades Across the Board
snippet: Jefferies analysts issued updated coverage on four buy-rated mining names positioned for the current copper and gold environment: Capstone Copper (2026 EPS raised to $0.53), Barrick Gold (premium asset base, compelling valuation), Endeavour Mining (full-year 2026 EPS forecast $6.36), and Kinross Gold (2026 gold-equivalent sales target 2,102 koz). The upgrades reflect a constructive view on both metals — gold miners continue to trade at historically wide discounts to NAV despite record prices, while COMEX copper net-long positioning has hit an all-time high ahead of the June 30 Section 232 tariff decision — a setup Jefferies believes sets up asymmetric upside for operationally reliable producers.
